findings.evidence: `nl -ba` shows `residueTheorem_aux` begins at line 138, the induction proof starts at line 143, and the proof body continues through the base case ending at line 217; the largest branch is lines 155-207.
findings.fix: Factor the pole case into one or more private lemmas, e.g. a `peelLeadingTerm`/`residueTheorem_step` lemma proving the depth decrease and integral/residue decomposition for `G := F - P`, leaving `residueTheorem_aux` as a short induction skeleton.
findings.issue: `residueTheorem_aux` runs from the strong-induction header through a 70+ line proof, with the whole pole-removal step, depth decrease, integrability transfer, and residue/integral algebra inline; this makes the reason the induction works hard to maintain and brittle under local API changes.

summary: The main residue theorem proof has one proof-quality issue: the induction step is too large and hides the pole-peeling argument inline.
